sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: DOMINANT UPPER RIDGE WILL REMAIN ANCHORED OVER THE SRN PLAINS THROUGH FRIDAY WITH A GRADUAL NWWD EXPANSION EXPECTED ACROSS THE ROCKIES. STRONGEST FLOW ALOFT WILL PERSIST ALONG THE U.S./CANADIAN BORDER WITH ANY MEANINGFUL HEIGHT FALLS OCCURRING AHEAD OF STRONG SHORTWAVE TROUGH ACROSS ONTARIO INTO THE NRN GREAT LAKES REGION. ACROSS MUCH OF THE COUNTRY POCKETS OF ASCENT WILL BE LOCALIZED...OFTEN LOOSELY TIED TO DECAYING MCSS FROM PREVIOUS DAY THUNDERSTORM CLUSTERS AND WITHIN UPSLOPE REGIONS OF THE PLAINS. AS A RESULT...THERE APPEARS TO BE A THREAT FOR ROBUST THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT GENERALLY ALONG SRN PERIPHERY OF STRONGER MID LEVEL FLOW FROM PORTIONS OF THE UPPER GREAT LAKES/MID MS VALLEY REGION WWD INTO PORTIONS OF THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS.

sections.title: UPPER GREAT LAKES/MID-LOWER MO VALLEY
sections.text: STRONG SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL EJECT ACROSS MANITOBA INTO ONTARIO LATE IN THE PERIOD WITH SEASONALLY STRONG MID LEVEL FLOW EXPECTED TO TRANSLATE THROUGH THE BASE OF THE TROUGH ACROSS MN INTO WI WHERE HIGH LEVEL FLOW SHOULD PROVE DIFFLUENT. MODELS ARE IN GENERAL AGREEMENT THAT CONVECTION WILL LIKELY EVOLVE ALONG SRN FRINGE OF STRONGER FORCING WITHIN THIS LARGE SCALE DIFFLUENCE. MCS ACTIVITY SHOULD BE ONGOING AT THE BEGINNING OF THE PERIOD ACROSS PORTIONS OF SRN MN/IA INTO PORTIONS OF WI...PRIMARILY DUE TO LOW LEVEL WARM ADVECTION. THIS ACTIVITY MAY NOT COMPLETELY DISSIPATE DURING THE DAY BUT RATHER SPREAD/DEVELOP EWD AHEAD OF MAIN COLD FRONT TOWARD LOWER MI WHERE INSTABILITY SHOULD BE CONSIDERABLY LESS THAN AREAS WEST OF LAKE MI. MUCH GREATER BUOYANCY WILL EXIST SWWD ACROSS WI/IA INTO MO AND ACROSS THE CNTRL PLAINS. HOWEVER LARGE SCALE FORCING WILL WANE NOTICEABLY ACROSS ERN NEB/KS. AT THIS TIME IT/S NOT ENTIRELY CLEAR HOW CONVECTION WILL EVOLVE ACROSS THE SLIGHT RISK REGION...PARTLY DUE TO UNCERTAINTY OF POTENTIAL MCS ACTIVITY EARLY IN THE PERIOD. BOTH THE GFS/NAM SUGGEST A POSSIBLE MCS WILL EVOLVE WITHIN THE WARM ADVECTION ZONE ACROSS THE LOWER MO VALLEY...HOWEVER MODELS TYPICALLY H

sections.title: CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: UPSLOPE FLOW WILL INCREASE MARKEDLY DURING THE PERIOD ACROSS THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS FROM WRN KS/NERN CO INTO SERN WY/NEB PANHANDLE. ESELY BOUNDARY LAYER FLOW WILL FORCE CONSIDERABLE MOISTURE WWD BENEATH UPPER RIDGE WHERE H5 WLY FLOW WILL BE ON THE ORDER OF 25-40KT. NEEDLESS TO SAY DEEP VEERING PROFILES OF SIGNIFICANT SHEAR WILL EXIST ACROSS THIS REGION DURING THE CONVECTIVE CYCLE. IT APPEARS SCATTERED SUPERCELLS WILL EVOLVE BY LATE AFTERNOON THEN PROPAGATE SEWD INTO A MODEST ESELY LLJ ON THE ORDER OF 30KT. MULTIPLE MCSS WILL LIKELY EVOLVE ACROSS THIS REGION DURING THE LATTER HALF OF THE PERIOD. A FEW TORNADOES COULD OCCUR EARLY WITH DISCRETE SUPERCELLS...OTHERWISE LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS ARE THE PRIMARY THREATS.

sections.title: FL
sections.text: SRN FRINGE OF OLD EAST COAST UPPER TROUGH WILL BECOME DETACHED ACROSS THE FL PENINSULA DURING THE PERIOD WITH A POCKET OF COOLER MID LEVEL TEMPERATURES FORECAST TO SETTLE ACROSS SOUTH FL. ANOTHER CONVECTIVELY-ACTIVE DAY SHOULD BE NOTED ACROSS THE PENINSULA...A FEW STORMS COULD PRODUCE LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS. ..DARROW/JEWELL.. 07/10/2009

sections.title: MID MS/LOWER MO RIVER VALLEYS INTO THE CENTRAL GREAT LAKES
sections.text: SIGNIFICANT SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL CONTINUE EWD ACROSS THE UPPER MS RIVER VALLEY/GREAT LAKES THROUGH TONIGHT...WHILE LOWER AMPLITUDE WAVES CONTINUE TO EJECT E AND THEN SE AROUND TOP OF SRN PLAINS UPPER LEVEL ANTICYCLONE. THIS WILL MAINTAIN BROAD BELT OF ENHANCED WLY MID AND UPPER LEVEL WINDS SPREADING FROM THE CENTRAL ROCKIES/PLAINS ACROSS MUCH OF THE MID WEST AND GREAT LAKES REGION DURING THE PERIOD. PRIMARY SURFACE COLD FRONT ASSOCIATED WITH NRN STREAM SYSTEM IS EXPECTED TO ADVANCE SEWD INTO THE NRN/WRN GREAT LAKES AND STALL E-W ACROSS NEB THIS AFTERNOON...WITH PRECEEDING WARM SECTOR BEING MUDDLED BY NUMEROUS SURFACE OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES FROM PRIOR CONVECTION. PRESENCE OF ONGOING MCS ACTIVITY AND DIVERSE SOLUTIONS BY OVERNIGHT MODELS MAKES SPECIFIC FORECASTING OF EVOLVING SEVERE THREAT QUITE DIFFICULT THIS MORNING. EXPECT INITIAL STRONG STORM CLUSTERS/MCSS TO WEAKEN SOME THROUGH THE MORNING AS LLJ DIMINISHES WITH MIXING BOUNDARY LAYER. HOWEVER...ISOLATED HAIL/WIND IN EXCESS OF SEVERE LEVELS REMAINS POSSIBLE WITH THESE STORMS. BY LATER TODAY...HEATING AND CONVERGENCE ALONG EITHER PRECEEDING SURFACE FEATURES AND/OR INVOF MAIN SURFACE COLD FRONT SHOULD FOCUS VIGOROUS CONVECTION CONTINU

sections.title: CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS INTO THE CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: INCREASING UPSLOPE FLOW AND DESTABILIZATION SHOULD INCREASE STRONG TO SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ALONG THE FRONT RANGE OF THE CENTRAL ROCKIES AND ADJACENT HIGH PLAINS DURING THE MID TO LATE AFTERNOON. DEEP LAYER SHEAR WILL BE QUITE STRONG AND LIKELY SUPPORT A FEW SUPERCELLS THROUGH THE EVENING...INCLUDING THE POTENTIAL FOR A TORNADO OR TWO. HOWEVER...LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE PRIMARY THREATS WITH THE MORE ORGANIZED STORMS. ACTIVITY COULD BUILD UPSCALE INTO A MCS OR NEW DEVELOPMENT MAY OCCUR EWD INTO THE CENTRAL PLAINS OVERNIGHT WITH ADDITIONAL RISK OR LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS.

sections.title: FL
sections.text: MORNING SOUNDINGS MAINTAIN UNSEASONABLY COOL MID LEVEL TEMPERATURES ACROSS FL ALONG SLOW MOVING PORTIONS OF MID LEVEL TROUGH WHICH HAS PERSISTED OVER THE EAST COAST THE PAST FEW DAYS. THE COLD AIR ALOFT WILL BOOST INSTABILITY TODAY ATOP MID 70F SURFACE DEW POINTS ...ALTHOUGH LINGERING CLOUDS ACROSS CENTRAL/SRN FL THIS MORNING WILL HINDER HEATING. STORMS ALREADY DEVELOPING NEAR SURFACE FRONT OVER NRN FL AND ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT EXPECTED INVOF SMALL SCALE OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES/SEA BREEZE CIRCULATIONS FARTHER SOUTH SHOULD BE CAPABLE OF ISOLATED LARGE HAIL/STRONG DOWNBURSTS TODAY. DESPITE THE PULSE-SEVERE THREAT...OVERALL LIMITED ORGANIZATION SHOULD HINDER COVERAGE/SEVERITY UNDER RELATIVELY WEAK FLOW ALOFT. ..EVANS/HURLBUT.. 07/10/2009

mesoscale_discussions.topic: HEAVY RAINFALL VALID 110830Z - 111000Z PRIMARY THREAT FROM ONGOING TSTMS LOCATED ACROSS EAST CENTRAL KS INTO WEST CENTRAL MO IS EXPECTED TO BE HEAVY RAINFALL RATES /UP TO 2 INCHES PER HOUR/ WITH STORMS TRAINING SEWD FROM THE VICINITY OF OJC INTO WEST CENTRAL TO SWRN MO. LOW LEVEL WAA ALONG THE NOSE OF A SWLY 40-50 KT LLJ EXTENDING INTO ERN KS/WRN MO COMBINED WITH ASCENT ATTENDANT TO A COUPLE OF WEAK MID LEVEL IMPULSES TRANSLATING ESEWD FROM KS TO THE MID MS VALLEY WILL LIKELY SUPPORT ADDITIONAL TSTM DEVELOPMENT IN DISCUSSION AREA. THE ONGOING TSTM ACTIVITY HAS BEEN FORMING ALONG AND JUST N/NE OF A WARM FRONT WHICH EXTENDED ESEWD FROM AN AREA OF LOW PRESSURE LOCATED IN SOUTH CENTRAL KS /25 W ICT/.
